note: This tree is NOT on disk. Lines come from the upstream tag on the web: github.com/Matthias-Wandel/jhead tag 3.06.0.1 = commit 78057ab, Apr 14 2021. They were computed, not read directly. I took the exact hunk headers of the GitHub compare afadc77...78057ab (afadc77 = 'Update version number to 3.04', confirmed identical to the local 3.04 tree at every hunk anchor) and applied the offsets to the verified 3.04 lines. Three cross-checks agree: ClearOrientation exif.c:1248 (issue #36 trace), shellescape jhead.c:345 / DoCommand call 393 (issue #51 trace), and gpsinfo Get32s at 144 (issue #99 trace on a later version). Verify against the real tree once it is fetched. Every 3.04 read bug that only over-reads a section by 20 bytes or less is masked here: since 5186ddc every JPEG section is malloc'd with 20 bytes of slack. That is why CVE-2020-6625, CVE-2018-6612, CVE-2026-90681 and CVE-2026-90682 are excluded for this version.

cves.trigger: Two APP1 Exif sections (or a malformed first 'Exif' section) with Orientation!=1 in the later one: DiscardAllButExif frees the section OrientationPtr points into, then ClearOrientation does Put16u(OrientationPtr,1) on freed memory
cves.fixed_in: upstream f0a8842 (Sep 2021, after this tag; in 3.08); Debian 1:3.06.0.1-5
cves.note: Line is from the web source (computed, and it matches issue #36's trace 'ClearOrientation exif.c:1248:17'). The call is from DoAutoRotate jhead.c (~725), after DiscardAllButExif in ProcessFile.

cves.trigger: JPEG with an end-of-exif thumbnail and a filename containing $(...), backticks or '"': the filename is put inside "..." unescaped in the mogrify command and run with system() (~line 788)
cves.note: Line is from the web source (computed: 3.04 line 776 + 9). Needs a crafted FILENAME, not file content. The same pattern is in DoAutoRotate's thumbnail jpegtran sprintf (~jhead.c:757, -autorot) and the -ce editor command (~jhead.c:167).

cves.trigger: -cmd with many &i/&o tokens and a long filename: each shellescape() bounds only its own output (j<PATH_MAX), so the expansions overrun DoCommand's stack buffer ExecString[PATH_MAX*3]
cves.note: Line is from the web source (computed, and it matches issue #51's trace shellescape jhead.c:345:25 / DoCommand jhead.c:393). The total must exceed 12288 bytes: use a filename of ~200+ chars with 70 &i (shown), or more tokens.

cves.trigger: GPS numeric tag with several components near the end of the Exif section under -v: PrintFormatNumber(ValuePtr+a*ComponentSize, Format, ByteCount) is called per component and each call prints up to ByteCount bytes. That reads well past the value, e.g. 4 URATIONALs over-read 24 bytes, more than the 20-byte slack
cves.note: Line is from the web source (computed: 3.04 line 208 + 6). The 3.08 report shows gpsinfo.c:215. The CVE was filed against 3.08, and the loop is unchanged between 3.04 and 3.08. The over-read can exceed the 20-byte slack, so it stays ASAN-visible.

cves.trigger: Exif date rewrite memcpy(ExifSection->Data + DateTimeOffsets[a] + 8, TempBuf, 19): offsets are collected from DateTime tags in every parsed Exif section but written into the first M_EXIF section, with no size bound
cves.note: Line is from the web source (computed: 3.04 line 1156 + 9). Filed against 3.08 as heap-use-after-free (CWE-416), where ASAN saw the write land in a freed realloc'd Sections array. df124a4, which is in this tag, rejects date tags within 19 bytes of the end of their own section. The cross-section (two Exif sections) variant is still open. This needs -ts/-ta/-ds/-dsft. I did not reproduce it.

excluded.reason: fixed by commits in the 3.06.0.1 tag (56c108f+a50953a, b711024, 5186ddc, 4827ed3, ca2973f, a50953a, b8d78e5, 556a0c5).

faulty code still present, but since 5186ddc every section is allocated with 20 spare bytes, so the over-reads stay in bounds and are invisible to ASan (Debian still lists 6624/6625 as unfixed/unimportant).
